title: Generic Relationships and Constraints knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is a central advantage of generics?
options: They preserve a relationship between input types and output types without defaulting to any.
They guarantee every runtime input is valid.
They only work for string values.
They remove the need for tests.
questions.answer_key: They preserve a relationship between input types and output types without defaulting to any.
questions.explanation: A well-designed generic preserves useful type information and constrains operations appropriately.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Generic Relationships and Constraints”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with relating input and output types and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with relating input and output types and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Relating input and output types”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Generic Relationships and Constraints”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check generic callbacks, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume constraints that preserve useful information is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check generic callbacks, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Generic callbacks”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
